events.status: Past — dates passed (21–27 Sep); held status not re-checked
events.detail: ADDED 21 SEPTEMBER 2026, THE DAY IT STARTED, AND WE OWN THE MISS — the 20 September evening MICE scan reported no new dated confirmation and did not have this. Kenya is hosting UN Tourism Week 2026 from 21 to 27 September. The Ministry of Tourism and Wildlife Management announced it in a Facebook statement on SATURDAY 19 SEPTEMBER, two days before it began: ‘From 21st–27th September, Kenya will welcome the global tourism community for UN Tourism Week 2026, a people-driven week celebrating the country’s culture, creativity and tourism experiences’ (People Daily, 19 September 2026). Stated focus is digital platforms, data-driven destination management, artificial intelligence and smart travel services, delivered through cultural showcases, live events, immersive storytelling and virtual engagement. NO VENUE, NO PROGRAMME DOCUMENT AND NO DELEGATE FIGURE HAVE BEEN PUBLISHED, and we estimate none. Note it closes on 27 September, the same day as World Tourism Day and Uganda’s national celebrations at Mbale. Ledger call P204 opened on whether any attendance figure or formal programme is ever published.
events.soWhat: Read this as a promotional and PR week, NOT a compression event: on the published evidence there is nothing here to block inventory against, and any Nairobi property that reprices on it is repricing on a Facebook post. The commercial value is visibility. If you have a sustainability, community-tourism or technology story, this is a seven-day window in which the Ministry is actively looking for Kenyan content to showcase, and the cost of pitching is an email. Two harder events in the same fortnight are the ones that actually move rooms: Kenya Transport Summit at KICC 30 September to 2 October, and Africa MICE Summit in Mombasa 1–2 October.
events.source: People Daily, 19 September 2026, reporting the Ministry of Tourism and Wildlife Management Facebook statement

events.event: World Tourism Day 2026 — Uganda national celebrations
events.status: Past — date passed (27 Sep); held status not re-checked
events.detail: Uganda's national World Tourism Day celebrations are being hosted at MBALE, in the eastern region, on 27 September 2026, immediately following UWA's Open Park Days of 25-27 September when entry to participating national parks and wildlife reserves is free. Participating parks: Murchison Falls, Queen Elizabeth, Lake Mburo and Kidepo Valley; reserves include Ajai, Katonga, Toro-Semuliki and Pian Upe. UWA Acting Commissioner for Tourism and Business Development Dorcus Rukundo framed the weekend as a domestic-travel push — 'You cannot promote what you have never experienced' — and UTB chief executive Juliana Kagwa described a deliberate strategy to decentralise tourism beyond the traditional park circuit toward Mount Elgon, Sipi Falls and the eastern cultural and coffee offer. The global 2026 theme is 'Digital Agenda and Artificial Intelligence to Redesign Tourism'. NO DELEGATE OR ATTENDANCE FIGURE HAS BEEN PUBLISHED and we estimate none. NOTE A SOURCE DISAGREEMENT ON ELIGIBILITY: July reporting described the free-entry window as open to everyone including international visitors, while the Daily Monitor's 5 September piece frames it as Ugandans; we have not seen a UWA notice settling it, so confirm eligibility with UWA before promising a rate to a foreign guest.
events.soWhat: Two different commercial events in one weekend, and they pull in opposite directions. Eastern Uganda — Mbale, Sipi Falls, Mount Elgon — gets a genuine, government-backed compression event with almost no branded room stock to absorb it: if you operate there, this is a rate weekend, and it is seven days out. For the main-circuit parks the waiver removes the entry fee but not transport, accommodation or activities, so Murchison, QENP, Lake Mburo and Kidepo should expect a domestic day-visitor surge rather than bed-nights — staff the gates and the restaurant, not the rooms, and push a paid add-on (boat cruise, guided walk, game drive) because that is where the margin still sits. Do not discount rooms into a weekend where the traffic is not sleeping over.
events.source: Daily Monitor, 5 September 2026 (UWA Open Park Days launch and World Tourism Day activities); UWA

events.status: Held — Nairobi, 8 October 2026 (Citizen Digital, 9 Oct 2026; Kenya Airways gala promotion page)
events.detail: UPDATED 9 NOVEMBER 2026: HELD. The inaugural gala, billed by its partners as the ‘Tatler Best Africa 2026 Awards Gala’, took place in Nairobi on Thursday 8 October 2026 during MKTE. Citizen Digital (Vincent Anguche, 9 Oct 2026, citizen.digital/article/15-kenyan-hotels-recognised-among-africas-best-n375360) reported the ceremony ‘tonight’ with Tourism CS Rebecca Miano quoted and 15 Kenyan hotels honoured; Kenya Airways’ official gala travel promotion (kenya-airways.com/en/promotions/tba-awards-gala-nbo-2026/, read 9 Nov 2026) gives 8 October 2026, Nairobi. No venue named by either source; no attendance figure published and none estimated. This supersedes our earlier ‘date unconfirmed’ label. ORIGINAL ENTRY: Kenya Tourism Board has signed a THREE-YEAR SUBVENTION AGREEMENT with Tatler Africa to bring the inaugural Tatler Best of Africa event to Kenya and to host the Tatler Africa office on the continent| framed inside a stated KSh 1 trillion tourism-GDP target (ATQ News| 9 September 2026). Several trade aggregators carry 8 October 2026 in Nairobi as the awards date| but we have NOT matched that date to a KTB or Tatler Group source| so it is logged as reported-not-confirmed. No delegate count published and none estimated.
events.soWhat: An awards night is a one- or two-night top-end city compression event| not a congress — but the strategic point outweighs the room nights. A national tourism board is now subsidising the platform that will shape which African properties get international luxury shelf space for three years. Top-end Nairobi| Laikipia and coast properties should ask KTB directly how shortlisting and nomination work| this quarter| rather than waiting to be discovered. Do not block inventory against the 8 October date until it is confirmed by KTB or Tatler.
events.source: Citizen Digital, 9 October 2026 (ceremony held in Nairobi); Kenya Airways Tatler Best Africa 2026 gala promotion page (8 Oct 2026, Nairobi), read 9 November 2026; ATQ News, 9 September 2026 (KTB–Tatler Africa subvention agreement, lead only)

events.event: Africa MICE Summit 2026 (incl. Africa MICE Awards & MICE Investors Round Table)
events.status: Past — dates passed (1–2 Oct); held status not re-checked
events.detail: NOTE THE MOVE. The 2025 edition ran 9–11 September in NAIROBI; the 2026 edition is 1–2 October in MOMBASA — anyone still holding the Nairobi September dates is holding last year’s diary. Theme: ‘Building Africa’s Business Events Ecosystem for Trade| Investment and Innovation’. Africa MICE Awards gala 2 October| 60+ categories. A MICE Investors & Stakeholders Round Table runs the same day| pitching convention-centre and exhibition-venue projects to investors and DFIs under an AfCFTA framing. Organised by Zuri Events. The 600+ figure is the organiser’s own attendance claim and covers the summit| not a verified registration count.
events.soWhat: Two nights| Mombasa| in the same week Kenya’s autumn conference calendar opens — and Mombasa is the county carrying Kenya’s heaviest dengue and mpox burden (3|989 dengue cases Jan–May; 452 mpox cases). Coast properties should hold rate 30 Sep–2 Oct rather than discounting into the shoulder| AND have the daytime vector protocol visibly in place before a room full of Africa’s business-events buyers arrives. This is the single audience most likely to notice. Right-size the block: 600+ is an organiser figure across two days| much of it Mombasa-based trade| so treat it as a venue-cluster event until registrations are published.
events.source: africamicesummit.org (organiser site, read 9 September 2026)

events.event: World Travel Awards — Grand Final Gala Ceremony 2026
events.city: Serengeti National Park (reported venue: Four Seasons Safari Lodge Serengeti)
events.status: Confirmed — date on WTA’s own events page; Serengeti venue double-sourced
events.delegates: More than 500 international guests expected (Tanzania Tourist Board, per Daily News, 6 Nov 2026); not a registration count
events.detail: UPDATED 9 NOVEMBER 2026: VENUE NAMED — SERENGETI, NOT DAR OR ZANZIBAR. WTA’s own 2026 Grand Tour page (worldtravelawards.com/events, read 9 Nov 2026) lists the Grand Final Gala Ceremony as ‘Tanzania, 12 December 2026’ with no city and ‘all dates and destinations subject to change’. The Serengeti National Park venue is reported by Daily News (TZ), 6 Nov 2026 (dailynews.co.tz/serengeti-makes-history-as-world-tourism-awards-host/), and by the Tanzania High Commission London’s tanzaniatourism.uk, 7 Nov 2026 (tanzaniatourism.uk/post/tanzania-to-host-world-travel-awards-grand-final-on-december-12th), which names the Four Seasons Safari Lodge Serengeti in central Serengeti (single-sourced lodge detail). The Respondents (6 Nov 2026) reports WTA founder Graham Cooke announced it on 5 Nov on the sidelines of WTM London. Daily News calls it the first WTA ceremony held inside a national park. Climax of WTA's Grand Tour 2026 and Tanzania's second WTA event of the year after the 28 August Africa Gala in Zanzibar.
events.soWhat: This is a bush-lodge event, not a city one: the compression lands on central Serengeti lodges and camps and on the Arusha / Seronera air links around 12 December, the start of the festive high season, not on Dar or Zanzibar city stock. Serengeti properties near Seronera should hold rate and protect air seats for 10–14 Dec; Arusha transit hotels should expect a pre/post night. The 500+ figure is a TTB expectation, not a count.
events.source: World Travel Awards events page (date), read 9 Nov 2026; Daily News (TZ), 6 Nov 2026; tanzaniatourism.uk (Tanzania High Commission, London), 7 Nov 2026; The Respondents, 6 Nov 2026

events.status: Rescheduled — confirmed on organiser site; first time in Uganda
events.delegates: No 2027 figure published by the organiser; Nairobi 2026 drew 450+ senior leaders (organiser figure)
events.detail: UPDATED 9 NOVEMBER 2026: DATES MOVED. The organiser’s own site (futurehospitality.com/africa, read 9 Nov 2026) states: ‘FHS Africa will now take place on 28–29 April 2027 at Speke Resort Munyonyo, Kampala, Uganda’ and ‘The summit was originally scheduled for 2–3 February 2027.’ The move aligns the summit with the Pearl of Africa Tourism Expo (POATE) and places it ahead of AFCON 2027 (ATTA, 23 Oct 2026, citing Breaking Travel News; lead only). POATE 2027 dates themselves not yet read at a UTB page. ORIGINAL ENTRY: Africa's leading hospitality investment and leadership forum moves to Uganda for the first time, after Nairobi hosted the 2026 edition (31 Mar–1 Apr, 450+ senior industry leaders, at the Radisson Blu Nairobi Upper Hill).
events.soWhat: Uganda's first time hosting FHS is a direct signal the region's investor and developer circuit is testing Kampala as a serious destination — read together with the Hilton and Marriott Kampala openings, this is exactly the kind of event that turns a one-off signing into a sustained pipeline. Kampala city hotels now have until late April, not February, to get corporate and long-stay rate structures ready — and anyone who blocked rooms or flights for 2–3 February should move them now. Late April also stacks FHS with POATE at the same Munyonyo venue, so the Munyonyo/Ggaba cluster should price that week as one event.
events.source: futurehospitality.com/africa (organiser), read 9 November 2026; ATTA, 23 October 2026 (lead); original: Breaking Travel News / ChimpReports / New Vision (UG)

events.city: Kigali (venue not named in the announcement coverage; Kigali Convention Centre presumed, not confirmed)
events.status: Bid won — first Africa host in 20 years
events.delegates: More than 2,000 delegates expected (Rwanda Convention Bureau, 7th-edition newsletter)
events.detail: RE-CHECKED 9 NOVEMBER 2026: dates 24–27 October 2027 unchanged, carried in ICCA’s announcement as reported by VoyagesAfriq (2 Feb 2026) and Cimunity (3 Feb 2026), both quoting RCB CEO Janet Karemera; the delegate figure is the Rwanda Convention Bureau’s own (rcb.rw/IMG/pdf/rcb_7th_edition_newsletter.pdf). Neither ICCA coverage nor RCB names the venue, so the earlier ‘Kigali Convention Centre’ is our presumption. ICCA’s own site (iccacongress.org) currently covers only the 65th Congress in Panama City, 8–11 November 2026 — expect a Kigali handover there this week. The International Congress and Convention Association's global congress returns to Africa for the first time in two decades. Brings together association representatives and industry leaders on growth strategy, capacity building and Africa's role in global business events.
events.soWhat: A 14-month lead time and a confirmed 2,000+ delegate congress at Rwanda's flagship convention venue is about as clean a forward booking signal as this region produces. Kigali hotels and DMCs should be building October 2027 into 2026/27 rate planning now, not waiting for the pre-event rush — this is exactly the kind of confirmed compression a ledger entry is for.
events.source: VoyagesAfriq, 2 Feb 2026; Cimunity, 3 Feb 2026; mice.net.au, 6 Feb 2026 (ICCA announcement); Rwanda Convention Bureau 7th-edition newsletter (delegates); re-checked 9 Nov 2026

events.city: Kigali (Kigali Convention Centre per Rwanda Convention Bureau listing; organiser names no venue)
events.status: Confirmed — organiser press release
events.detail: RE-CHECKED 9 NOVEMBER 2026: DATES CORRECTED from 18–20 to 18–19 November. The organiser’s own press release (Africa Fintech Summit, Lagos, 2 Dec 2025; africafintechsummit.com/uploads/press-releases/press-release-1764706211682-336823906.pdf) says the 16th edition ‘will head to … Kigali, Rwanda – on November 18-19, 2026’, with no venue named. The Rwanda Convention Bureau page (rcb.rw/Africa-Fintech-Summit.html, read 9 Nov 2026) lists ‘16th–19th Nov’ at Kigali Convention Centre with no year; the 18–20 range appears only in listings (Financial Afrik, 7 Sep 2026; FintechWeekly). The organiser’s main site did not render its event details. The largest bi-annual gathering of Africa's fintech ecosystem — regulators, policymakers, financial-industry executives, fintech founders, investors and startups — returns to the Kigali Convention Centre. Founded 2017; format runs keynotes, workshops, an awards ceremony, exhibition and startup pitch. No official delegate count published for the Kigali edition.
events.soWhat: A two-day continental fintech congress at KCC in mid-November is a genuine city-compression event for Kigali, drawing a pan-African regulator-and-investor crowd into the low-season shoulder. It also lands in the SAME week Uganda Airlines launches its daily Entebbe–Kigali service (18 Nov) — twin demand signals on the same dates. Kigali city hotels should hold corporate rate across 17–20 Nov rather than discounting into November.
events.source: Africa Fintech Summit press release, 2 Dec 2025 (organiser; dates); rcb.rw/Africa-Fintech-Summit.html (venue), read 9 Nov 2026

events.status: Held
events.detail: Rwanda's annual gorilla-naming ceremony, organised by the Rwanda Development Board at the foothills of Volcanoes National Park in Kinigi. Draws heads of state, conservationists, celebrities and diplomats; the flagship event of Rwanda's premium gorilla-tourism calendar. RDB formally unveiled the 21st-edition plans on 11 Aug 2026: 22 baby gorillas to be named.

Gorilla-trekking and exclusive-use inventory around Musanze should hold rate through the first week of September rather than discounting into the shoulder; Kigali city hotels should expect a pre/post-ceremony bump.
events.source: Rwanda Development Board / Taarifa, 11 Aug 2026 / kwitaizina.rw

events.status: Bid won — first World Athletics Championships on African soil
events.detail: World Athletics announced on 15 September 2026, after a Council meeting in Budapest, that Nairobi will host the 2029 World Athletics Championships — the first time the sport's flagship global event goes to Africa. Nairobi beat London and Rome for 2029; Munich was awarded 2031. The bid is centred on Moi International Sports Centre, Kasarani. President Sebastian Coe called the Nairobi bid a compelling proposition. NO delegate, athlete, official or spectator figure has been published and none is estimated here; competition dates are not yet fixed.
events.soWhat: A three-year runway on the largest single city-wide compression event Nairobi has ever been awarded. Nothing to price yet — but two things start now. First, any 2027-29 refinancing or refurbishment case for Nairobi city stock should be built with this in it, and the Fed's 16 September move to 3.75-4.00% means that case gets tested at a higher cost of capital than it would have three months ago. Second, Nairobi now has three dated major-event anchors in five years — AFCON co-hosting in June-July 2027 and this in 2029 — which is the argument for a convention-and-events rate strategy rather than an opportunistic one.
events.source: World Athletics press release / Daily Nation / The Star / ESPN, 15 September 2026

events.city: Kenya, Uganda and Tanzania (host cities per CAF)
events.status: Confirmed — hosts, kick-off and final dates (CAF); opening-match and final host country not yet named; CAF has flagged accommodation and single-visa gaps; no published accommodation framework
events.detail: UPDATED 9 NOVEMBER 2026: CAF’s own release of 2 May 2026 (cafonline.com, ‘Road to East Africa’) fixes kick-off Saturday 19 June and the final Saturday 17 July 2027, and says CAF ‘will announce the Country that will host the Opening Match and the Final in due course’ — no announcement found as at 9 Nov. NEW: on 30 October 2026 CAF published that it and the Uganda Tourism Board have concluded a partnership giving Uganda Tourism ‘Official Destination Sponsor rights’ for AFCON PAMOJA 2027 across broadcast, digital and in-stadium platforms under ‘Explore Uganda – The Pearl of Africa’, launched in Kampala (cafonline.com, published 30 Oct 2026). No fee disclosed; CAF’s ‘over 3 billion’ is a global reach claim, not attendance. UTB CEO Juliana Kagwa: ‘the biggest tourism marketing opportunity Uganda has had in a generation.’ Still no fan, delegate or room-night figure and no accommodation framework. UPDATED 23 SEPTEMBER 2026: on 22 September a CAF delegation led by Secretary General Samson Adamu, with Country Infrastructure Manager Bianca Wambui, briefed President Museveni at State House Entebbe after inspecting Uganda’s venues. Stadiums and training grounds were praised; accommodation outside Kampala and slow progress on a single three-country visa were flagged (Daily Monitor, 22 Sep; The EastAfrican, 23 Sep). Museveni: ‘The Kampala area has the facilities, but now the challenge is upcountry.’ Kick-off confirmed as 19 June 2027; Uganda venues Mandela National Stadium, Hoima City Stadium (~95% complete) and Akii-Bua Olympic Stadium, Lira (~80%) (Nile Post, 22 Sep). A CAF inspection report cited by the Daily Monitor reportedly requires at least five five-star hotels of 50+ rooms for teams and officials; seven hotels in Hoima and three in Masindi have been selected, backed by a reported Shs101.1bn UDB credit facility (Kawowo, 22 Sep; Reported). STILL no published room-block, rate-cap or allocation framework, and still NO fan, delegate or room-night figure from CAF or any host board; none estimated here. ORIGINAL ENTRY: Uganda co-hosts AFCON 2027 with Kenya and Tanzania in June and July 2027. Logged here on 17 September 2026 because French and European buyers were already discussing AFCON-linked multi-country itineraries with Ugandan operators at IFTM Top Resa in Paris on 16 September 2026 (Embassy of Uganda in Paris, via UG Standard and SoftPower News). NO delegate, fan or room-night figure has been published by CAF or by any of the three host tourism boards, and none is estimated here. As at this entry, we have found NO published room-block, rate-cap or accommodation-allocation framework for any host city.
events.soWhat: 23 SEP READ: US World Cup evidence (HVS, 7 Aug and 22 Sep 2026) says big tournaments are rate events, not occupancy events — occupancy fell below baseline in 7 of 11 US host cities while ADR rose in all, and group business was displaced. For Kampala, Nairobi and Dar: protect contracted safari and group nights, price match eves rather than the whole month. For Hoima and Masindi: underwrite new rooms on 2028 demand, not June 2027. The tournament lands at the front of the July–September high season in three countries at once, and the buyer conversation has started eight months before any host-side accommodation framework exists. Decide your own block-versus-transient split before a tour operator decides it for you, and do not contract 2027 group business on the assumption that a rate cap will not arrive. Also relevant to the bush product: an AFCON itinerary sold in Paris is a city-plus-safari itinerary, which is why gorilla permit allocation came up in the same meetings.
events.source: CAF (cafonline.com), 2 May 2026 (dates) and 30 October 2026 (UTB Official Destination Sponsor), read 9 November 2026; Embassy of Uganda in Paris, via UG Standard and SoftPower News, 16 September 2026; Daily Monitor and Nile Post, 22 September 2026; The EastAfrican, 23 September 2026

data.caveat: Coverage favours large, publicly announced trade and business-events gatherings picked up by tourism boards, convention bureaux and trade press — it under-represents smaller academic, medical and association congresses that book a single hotel rather than a citywide block. A missing event here is not evidence one isn't happening; check directly with KICC, Rwanda Convention Bureau, JNICC (Dar) or your local convention bureau for anything sector-specific.
